results.name: Vexev Raises $6M to Accelerate U.S. Commercialization of Autonomous Vascular Imaging Platform - BioSpace
results.content:
*Funding follows successful results in U.S. clinical study and advances FDA regulatory activities for VxWave, an AI-powered robotic ultrasound platform designed to expand access to standardized vascular imaging.*  
SYDNEY, Aug. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Australian medical robotics company [Vexev](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4744638-1&h=3745106719&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.vexev.com%2F&a=Vexev)today announced it has raised $6 million in new funding to accelerate the path to FDA 510(k) clearance and U.S. commercialization of VxWave, its robotic tomographic ultrasound platform, designed to improve access to standardized vascular imaging. The raise brings Vexev's total funding to date to $19 million.  
Cardiovascular disease is the world's leading cause of death, claiming nearly 20 million lives each year.1Yet access to high-quality vascular imaging remains constrained by specialist availability and inconsistent image acquisition. Vexev is developing autonomous robotic imaging technology designed to help address that challenge.  
VxWave combines robotics, artificial intelligence and ultrasound imaging to automate vascular ultrasound acquisition. The platform is being developed for upper-limb imaging, with dialysis vascular access as its initial application, where patients require frequent vascular monitoring and healthcare providers face increasing demand for efficient, standardized imaging.
Beyond dialysis vascular access, Vexev intends to expand its autonomous imaging platform into additional vascular disease applications like cardiovascular and peripheral artery disease, while building the clinical evidence needed to support future AI-enabled decisions.  
The fundraise round included participation from existing investors Blackbird Ventures, Neotribe Ventures, Startmate and Horizon, together with new investors TreeArc Investment Group, TEN13, Bioshore Ventures and Alumni Ventures. Funding will support regulatory activities, manufacturing scale-up and commercialization.  
"Having worked closely with Vexev for several years, I have seen the development of its impressive robot- and AI-based techniques for vascular imaging," said Anupam Agarwal, MD, Senior Vice President for Medicine and Dean of the Marnix E. Heersink School of Medicine at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, and past president of the American Society of Nephrology. "The company's initial focus on dialysis vascular access addresses an important challenge for patients and providers, and I believe this technology has the potential to bring meaningful innovation to dialysis patients with vascular access challenges."
**About Vexev** Vexev is an Australian medical robotics company that develops advanced vascular imaging technology designed to make high-quality scanning more accessible, consistent and scalable. Built by experts in vascular fluid dynamics and computational imaging, Vexev's mission is to improve vascular care by building the next generation of imaging and intelligence tools for clinicians and healthcare providers. Its lead product, VxWave, is being developed as an upper limb vascular imaging platform, with dialysis vascular access serving as its initial application as the company advances toward U.S. commercialization. Learn more at [www.vexev.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4744638-1&h=159291330&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.vexev.com%2F&a=www.vexev.com).  
**Regulatory Statement** VxWave Ultrasound Imaging System is an investigational device and has not been cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for commercial sale in the United States or by any other regulatory authority for commercial distribution.

results.name: Medical Robotics Startup Vexev Secures $8.6M - Inspirepreneur Magazine
results.content:
# Medical Robotics Startup Vexev Secures $8.6M  
#### Synopsis  
The UNSW spinout is accelerating US regulatory approval and commercial rollout of its VxWave tomographic ultrasound technology after lifting total funding to $27 million.  
Sydney-based medical robotics start-up Vexev has raised a $8.6m funding round, to fast-track its U.S. regulatory approval and commercialization of its VxWave ultrasound platform.  
Blackbird Ventures is among the investors that have backed Vexev in the past. It is a privately held firm, and therefore does not publicise revenue or profit figures.  
With the new funding, Vexev's total raised capital increases to $27 million and will be used for expanding its manufacturing capabilities and development of its products along with getting approval from the regulators.  
Vexev was established in 2018 as a spinout of the University of New South Wales (UNSW), where they're developing automated vascular imaging robotic ultrasound systems for dialysis patients.  
It specialises in technology that lets healthcare workers carry out vascular scans with minimal need to rely on specialist sonographers.
## **Clinical Progress Supports Expansion**  
The funding follows results from Vexev's CANSCAN clinical study, conducted at three dialysis centres in San Antonio, Texas. In the trial, 115 patients with advanced kidney disease were recruited and the scan completion rate was 94% and the data adequacy was 100% with scans being performed by existing dialysis clinic staff.  
The company also enrolled 120 patients in a larger feasibility study with the U.S. Renal Care, a leading dialysis provider in the U.S. The studies are part of the company's clinical evidence that it intends to use for its regulatory pathway in the United States.
## **Medical Imaging Market Continues to Grow**  
The new round of funding for Vexev is the latest contribution in a steady stream of investment for medical imaging around the world. Fortune Business Insights projects that the medical imaging market is expected to grow from US$41.63 billion in 2024 to US$67.15 billion by 2032, marking a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.2%.  
North America continues to be the largest market for medical imaging technologies because of the high healthcare costs and existing diagnostic infrastructure. Europe is the second largest regional market, and the Asia-Pacific market is projected to experience the highest growth rate, as a result of higher investments in healthcare in Australia, China, India, Japan, and South Korea.  
Source: Capital Brief  
Pooja Malik is a business journalist with over six years of experience covering startups, entrepreneurship, and emerging trends. She has previously worked with leading media platforms such as YourStory Media and BW BusinessWorld, where she reported on business, policy, and market developments. Currently, she serves as Editor at The Inspirepreneur Magazine, where she writes and edits stories across business, lifestyle, and travel, with a focus on clarity, accuracy, and reader relevance.

results.content:
# Vexev Raises Funds to Support VxWave Autonomous Vascular Imaging Platform  
## KEY TAKEAWAYS  
- Vexev raised $6 million in new funding to advance FDA 510(k) clearance and United States commercialization of its VxWave robotic tomographic ultrasound platform.
- The financing brings the company’s total funding to $19 million.
- In the CANSCAN feasibility trial, VxWave achieved a 94% scanning success rate for autonomous vascular imaging by nonspecialist clinical staff.  
August 11, 2026—Vexev, an Australia-based medical robotics company, announced it has raised $6 million in new funding to accelerate the path to FDA 510(k) clearance and United States commercialization of its VxWave robotic tomographic ultrasound platform, which is designed to improve access to standardized vascular imaging.  
The company advised that the financing round included participation from existing investors Blackbird Ventures, Neotribe Ventures, Startmate, and Horizon, together with new investors TreeArc Investment Group, TEN13, Bioshore Ventures, and Alumni Ventures. The company stated that the new round brings Vexev’s total funding to date to $19 million.  
According to Vexev, VxWave combines robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), and ultrasound imaging to automate vascular ultrasound acquisition. The platform is being developed for upper limb imaging, with dialysis vascular access as its initial application.
In November 2025, Vexev along with U.S. Renal Care [announced](https://evtoday.com/news/canscan-feasibility-trial-evaluates-semiautonomous-vascular-mapping-with-vexev-vxwave-imaging-system) the results of the [CANSCAN](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06691672) feasibility trial of the VxWave system.  
The company noted that in the CANSCAN study, VxWave demonstrated a 94% scanning success rate for autonomous vascular imaging by nonspecialist clinical staff, with the potential ability to standardize vascular imaging designed to improve consistency and potentially decrease time to diagnosis and treatment.  
Vexev stated that it intends to expand its autonomous imaging platform beyond dialysis vascular access into additional vascular disease applications like cardiovascular and peripheral artery disease, while building the clinical evidence needed to support future AI-enabled decisions.  
“Having worked closely with Vexev for several years, I have seen the development of its impressive robot- and AI-based techniques for vascular imaging,” commented Anupam Agarwal, MD, in the Vexev press release. “The company’s initial focus on dialysis vascular access addresses an important challenge for patients and providers, and I believe this technology has the potential to bring meaningful innovation to dialysis patients with vascular access challenges.”

results.name: Vexev Raises $6M to Advance VxWave Robotic Vascular Ultrasound in the U.S.
results.content:
Australian medical robotics company Vexev has raised $6 million to advance regulatory, manufacturing and commercialization activities for its AI-enabled robotic vascular ultrasound platform in the U.S. The latest financing brings the company’s total funding to $19 million.  
Vexev develops VxWave, a platform combining robotics, artificial intelligence and ultrasound imaging to automate the acquisition of diagnostic images and blood flow data from veins and arteries. The technology uses high-frequency sound waves to capture vascular ultrasound data while reducing reliance on manual image acquisition.  
The platform supports upper-limb imaging, with Vexev initially focusing on dialysis vascular access. Patients receiving dialysis require regular monitoring of their vascular access sites, creating a use case for more consistent and accessible imaging.  
Vexev plans to use the new capital to accelerate its work toward U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance, while supporting manufacturing capabilities and preparations for commercial deployment in the U.S.  
The company also intends to expand VxWave beyond dialysis vascular access into additional vascular conditions, including cardiovascular and peripheral artery disease.
"We believe high-quality vascular imaging should be available wherever patients receive care, not only when a specialist is available," John Carroll, cofounder and CEO of Vexev, said in a statement. "We are starting with dialysis patients because the clinical need is clear, but our vision is much broader: to build an autonomous imaging platform that helps clinicians make faster, more consistent and more informed decisions across vascular disease."  
Vexev is developing its platform within a broader market for AI-enabled vascular imaging and care coordination. Elucid provides AI-based imaging analysis software focused on cardiovascular disease and raised $80 million in Series C financing in 2023, bringing its reported total funding to $121 million.  
Viz.ai also operates in the vascular technology market through Viz Vascular, an AI platform designed to support vascular care coordination. The company raised $100 million in Series D financing, following a previous $71 million Series C round. That Series D brought Viz.ai’s reported total funding to $250 million and valued the company at $1.2 billion.  
Vexev’s latest financing will now support its progression toward FDA clearance and the operational requirements needed to introduce VxWave to the U.S. market.

# Vexev Raises A$8.6 Million to Advance Australian-Built Robotic Ultrasound Platform in the United States  
SYDNEY, Australia, August 7, 2026 - Australian medical robotics company [Vexev](https://www.vexev.com/) today announced it has raised A$8.6 million in new funding to accelerate the path to FDA 510(k) clearance and U.S. commercialisation of VxWave, its robotic tomographic ultrasound platform.  
The fundraise follows successful results in a multi-site clinical study conducted with U.S. Renal Care across dialysis clinics in Texas and will support regulatory activities, manufacturing scale-up and commercial preparation. The raise brings Vexev’s total funding to A$27 million (USD$19 million).  
Australia has a strong history of translating local research and engineering expertise into globally adopted medical technologies. Vexev is part of the next generation leading that capability and intends to expand its manufacturing operations for the advanced robotic medical imaging platform in Surry Hills ahead of rollout to the one of the largest healthcare markets in the United States.  
Cardiovascular disease is the world's leading cause of death, claiming nearly 20 million lives each year.¹ Yet access to high-quality vascular imaging remains constrained by specialist availability and inconsistent image acquisition.
## About Vexev  
Vexev is an Australian-based medical robotics company that develops advanced vascular imaging technology designed to make high-quality scanning more accessible, consistent and scalable. Built by experts in vascular fluid dynamics and computational imaging, Vexev’s mission is to improve vascular care by building the next generation of imaging and intelligence tools for clinicians and healthcare providers. Its lead product, VxWave Ultrasound Imaging System, is being developed as an upper limb vascular imaging platform, with dialysis vascular access serving as its initial application as the company advances toward U.S. commercialisation. Learn more at [www.vexev.com](https://www.vexev.com/).
## Regulatory Statement  
VxWave Ultrasound Imaging System is an investigational device and has not been cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for commercial sale in the United States or by any other regulatory authority for commercial distribution.
